title: Patient Hardship Discount Program Sliding Fee Discount Schedule
content:
The Patient Hardship Discount Program grants its discount at one of six levels. Four levels are set by household income measured as a percentage of the federal poverty guideline, one limits what the patient pays to a share of annual household income, and one is granted on current enrollment in a public benefit program.

## Schedule of discount levels

| Level | Household income band, as % of the poverty guideline | Discount removed from each eligible patient-responsibility charge | Most the patient pays during the eligibility period, as % of annual household income | Public benefit programs that qualify without income documents |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) | 301 to 400 | 25% | 0 (not a catastrophic level) | None (income-tested level) |
| Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) | 251 to 300 | 50% | 0 (not a catastrophic level) | None (income-tested level) |
| Hardship Discount Level 3 (75%) | 201 to 250 | 75% | 0 (not a catastrophic level) | None (income-tested level) |
| Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) | 0 to 200 (no lower bound) | 100% | 0 (not a catastrophic level) | None (income-tested level) |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship | 0 to 600 (no lower bound) | 0 (the catastrophic cap applies instead) | 20% | None (income-tested level) |
| Presumptive Eligibility Discount | Lowest 0 and highest 0: income is not tested | 100% | 0 (not a catastrophic level) | SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP, homeless shelter |

## Notes to the schedule

1. **Band figures.** The lowest figure of a band is the lowest household income, as a whole percentage of the federal poverty guideline, for that level; a lowest figure of 0 means the level has no lower bound. The highest figure is the highest household income for the level; a highest figure of 0 means income is not tested at that level.
2. **Discount percentage.** The percentage is the share of each eligible patient-responsibility charge that the discount removes. A percentage of 0 marks the level that uses the catastrophic cap instead of a percentage.
3. **Catastrophic share.** The share is the most of the household's annual income that the patient pays during the eligibility period. A share of 0 marks a level that is not catastrophic.
4. **Qualifying programs.** The programs listed are public benefit programs whose current enrollment qualifies the applicant without income documents. The column is empty at every income-tested level.

## The schedule read by question

- *Which levels remove a fixed percentage of each charge?* Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%), Level 2 (50%), Level 3 (75%), Level 4 (100%) and the Presumptive Eligibility Discount (100%).
- *Which level limits the patient's total instead?* Catastrophic Medical Hardship, at 20% of annual household income during the eligibility period; its discount percentage is 0.
- *Which level is not tested against income?* The Presumptive Eligibility Discount, whose band figures are both 0 and whose qualifying programs are SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP and homeless shelter.
- *Where do the income-tested bands meet?* Level 4 ends at 200 and Level 3 begins at 201; Level 3 ends at 250 and Level 2 begins at 251; Level 2 ends at 300 and Level 1 begins at 301; Level 1 ends at 400.
